cases.name: percentile_rank_ties_below
cases.working: values strictly below 2: only 1, so 1 of 5 = 0.2

cases.name: percentile_rank_ties_at_or_below
cases.working: values at or below 2: 1, 2, 2, so 3 of 5 = 0.6

cases.name: percentile_rank_under_all
cases.working: no value is at or below 0: 0 of 5 = 0

cases.name: percentile_rank_ramp_252_below
cases.working: the values are 1..252 (252 values); strictly below 100 are 1..99, which is 99 values; 99/252 = 0.392857142857

cases.name: percentile_rank_ramp_252_at_or_below
cases.working: the values are 1..252; at or below 100 are 1..100, which is 100 values; 100/252 = 0.396825396825

cases.name: rolling_mean_window_3
cases.working: null marks warm-up (NaN) for the first window-1 = 2 entries; (1+2+3)/3 = 2; (2+3+4)/3 = 3; (3+4+5)/3 = 4

cases.name: rolling_std_dev_window_2
cases.working: window [1,2]: mean 1.5, sum of squares 0.5, /(2-1), sqrt = 0.70710678; window [2,4]: mean 3, sum of squares 2, /1, sqrt = 1.41421356; entry 0 is warm-up

cases.name: rolling_min_window_3
cases.working: min(3,1,4) = 1; min(1,4,1) = 1; min(4,1,5) = 1; two warm-up entries

cases.name: rolling_max_window_3
cases.working: max(3,1,4) = 4; max(1,4,1) = 4; max(4,1,5) = 5; two warm-up entries

cases.name: rolling_percentile_rank_below
cases.working: entry i is the rank of values[i] among the window values[i-2..i], the entry itself in the window; i=2: window [1,3,2], x=2, below: {1} = 1/3; i=3: window [3,2,3], x=3, below: {2} = 1/3; i=4: window [2,3,5], x=5, below: {2,3} = 2/3
